# Independent audit: canonical simplex physical Hessian


including its Section 4 feasibility and rank assertions.

I independently expanded the exact cut-simplex edge-ratio formula.
The determinant represents the physical d-dimensional volume because
the barycentric matrix acts identically on the one-dimensional quotient
by the direction hyperplane. Log differentiation gives precisely
F_i'/(Gamma V)=tr B+row_i B and the stated second derivative. Cancellation
of the trace terms yields

    Q=||column A||^2/d
           -(||row A||^2+||A||_F^2)/(d+1).

The prescribed-column least-cost problem has the displayed unique
stationary lift. Its zero-sum and constant components are orthogonal,
as is the zero-column remainder. The signs and dimensions are therefore
exactly d positive, one zero and d^2-1 negative, for every d>=2.
No argument here extends that inertia assertion to d=1.

For the shared m-cap system, translations give all zero-sum first cap
derivatives and a centroid dilation gives the common derivative, so
the full first-cap map is onto R^m. The positive critical direction
exists by the stated dimension bound. Its acceleration can set every
cap second derivative to -epsilon. The objective's second derivative
is the positive Lagrangian second derivative minus epsilon/Gamma,
with the factor and sign as stated. The smooth rational formula and
the explicit open compatibility hypothesis then give an actual
strict improvement preserving every fixed budget.

I reran supporting computation verify_canonical_simplex_hessian_inertia.py with the math-venv
Python runtime. It passed 25 exact physical-Hessian/lift tests,
full ranks, null modes and positive-subspace coefficients in dimensions
2 through 6. The theorem's all-dimensional claim follows from the
algebraic proof, not these finite checks.

A separate extension and its necessary qualifications are saved in
aligned-canonical-cap-blocks-second-order-rank-and-stress.md. Complete
canonical tuples give rank at most dh on the dN positive modes.
With full traces retained, a local maximum must admit SOME normal
stress with positive proper-cap weight on at most h selected fibers.
One arbitrary first stress with larger support is not sufficient to
force descent. No correction to the audited source note was needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
